[**1\. Calling the API**](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api#api-call)

- [Install the client](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api#api-call-install)

[**5\. Schema**](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api#schema)

- [Input](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api#schema-input)
- [Output](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api#schema-output)
- [Other](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api#schema-other)

### About

Realtime audio conversation over WebSocket.

### 1\. Calling the API [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#api-call-install)

### Install the client [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#api-call-install)

The client provides a convenient way to interact with the model API.

npmyarnpnpmbun

```
npm install --save @fal-ai/client
```

##### Migrate to @fal-ai/client

The `@fal-ai/serverless-client` package has been deprecated in favor of `@fal-ai/client`. Please check the [migration guide](https://docs.fal.ai/clients/javascript#migration-from-serverless-client-to-client) for more information.

### Setup your API Key [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#api-call-setup)

Set `FAL_KEY` as an environment variable in your runtime.

```
export FAL_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
```

### Real-time via WebSockets [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#api-call-realtime)

This model has a real-time mode via websockets, this is supported via the `fal.realtime` client.

```
import { fal } from "@fal-ai/client";

const connection = fal.realtime.connect("fal-ai/personaplex/realtime", {
  onResult: (result) => {
    console.log(result);
  },
  onError: (error) => {
    console.error(error);
  },
  // Fetch short-lived JWT token from your backend
  tokenProvider: async (app) => {
    const response = await fetch("/api/fal/realtime-token", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ app }),
    });
    return response.text();
  },
  tokenExpirationSeconds: 10,
});

connection.send({
  audio: ""
});
```

## 2\. Authentication [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#auth)

The API uses an API Key for authentication. It is recommended you set the `FAL_KEY` environment variable in your runtime when possible.

### API Key [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#auth-api-key)

In case your app is running in an environment where you cannot set environment variables, you can set the API Key manually as a client configuration.

```
import { fal } from "@fal-ai/client";

fal.config({
  credentials: "YOUR_FAL_KEY"
});
```

##### Protect your API Key

When running code on the client-side (e.g. in a browser, mobile app or GUI applications), make sure to not expose your `FAL_KEY`. Instead, **use a server-side proxy** to make requests to the API. For more information, check out our [server-side integration guide](https://docs.fal.ai/model-endpoints/server-side).

## 4\. Files [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#files)

Some attributes in the API accept file URLs as input. Whenever that's the case you can pass your own URL or a Base64 data URI.

### Data URI (base64) [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#files-data-uri)

You can pass a Base64 data URI as a file input. The API will handle the file decoding for you. Keep in mind that for large files, this alternative although convenient can impact the request performance.

### Hosted files (URL) [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#files-from-url)

You can also pass your own URLs as long as they are publicly accessible. Be aware that some hosts might block cross-site requests, rate-limit, or consider the request as a bot.

### Uploading files [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#files-upload)

We provide a convenient file storage that allows you to upload files and use them in your requests. You can upload files using the client API and use the returned URL in your requests.

```
import { fal } from "@fal-ai/client";

const file = new File(["Hello, World!"], "hello.txt", { type: "text/plain" });
const url = await fal.storage.upload(file);
```

##### Auto uploads

The client will auto-upload the file for you if you pass a binary object (e.g. `File`, `Data`).

Read more about file handling in our [file upload guide](https://docs.fal.ai/model-endpoints#file-uploads).

## 5\. Schema [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#schema)

### Input [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#schema-input)

`voice``VoiceEnum`

Voice ID for the AI response. NAT = natural, VAR = variety. F = female, M = male. Ignored when voice\_audio\_url is provided. Default value: `"NATF2"`

Possible enum values: `NATF0, NATF1, NATF2, NATF3, NATM0, NATM1, NATM2, NATM3, VARF0, VARF1, VARF2, VARF3, VARF4, VARM0, VARM1, VARM2, VARM3, VARM4`

`temperature_text``float`

Text sampling temperature. Higher values produce more diverse outputs. Default value: `0.7`

`voice_audio_url``string`

URL to a voice sample audio for on-the-fly voice cloning. When provided, the AI responds in the cloned voice instead of the preset 'voice'. 10+ seconds of clear speech recommended. Billed at 2x rate. Default value: `"null"`

`top_k_audio``integer`

Top-K sampling for audio tokens. Default value: `250`

`seed``integer`

Random seed for reproducibility.

`temperature_audio``float`

Audio sampling temperature. Higher values produce more diverse outputs. Default value: `0.8`

`prompt``string`

Text prompt describing the AI persona and conversation context. Default value: `"You are a wise and friendly teacher. Answer questions or provide advice in a clear and engaging way."`

`audio``string`\\* required

Input audio chunk (PCM s16le, 24kHz mono). Base64-encoded in JSON transport.

`top_k_text``integer`

Top-K sampling for text tokens. Default value: `25`

```
{
  "voice": "NATF2",
  "temperature_text": 0.7,
  "top_k_audio": 250,
  "temperature_audio": 0.8,
  "prompt": "You work for SwiftPlex Appliances which is a appliance repair company and your name is Farhod Toshmatov. Information: The dishwasher model is out of stock for replacement parts; we can use an alternative part with a 3-day delay. Labor cost remains $60 per hour.",
  "audio": "",
  "top_k_text": 25
}
```

### Output [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#schema-output)

`text``string`

Generated text tokens for this chunk. Default value: `""`

`audio``string`\\* required

Generated audio chunk (PCM s16le, 24kHz mono). Base64-encoded in JSON transport.

```
{
  "audio": ""
}
```

### Other types [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#schema-other)

#### File [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#type-File)

`url``string`\\* required

The URL where the file can be downloaded from.

`content_type``string`

The mime type of the file.

`file_name``string`

The name of the file. It will be auto-generated if not provided.

`file_size``integer`

The size of the file in bytes.

# fal-ai/personaplex/realtime

Realtime

PersonaPlex is a real-time, full-duplex speech-to-speech conversational model that enables persona control through text-based role prompts and audio-based voice conditioning.

- [Output](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api#schema-output)
- [Other](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api#schema-other)

### About

Realtime audio conversation over WebSocket.

### 1\. Calling the API [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#api-call-install)

### Install the client [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#api-call-install)

The client provides a convenient way to interact with the model API.

npmyarnpnpmbun

```
npm install --save @fal-ai/client
```

##### Migrate to @fal-ai/client

The `@fal-ai/serverless-client` package has been deprecated in favor of `@fal-ai/client`. Please check the [migration guide](https://docs.fal.ai/clients/javascript#migration-from-serverless-client-to-client) for more information.

### Setup your API Key [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#api-call-setup)

Set `FAL_KEY` as an environment variable in your runtime.

```
export FAL_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
```

### Real-time via WebSockets [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#api-call-realtime)

This model has a real-time mode via websockets, this is supported via the `fal.realtime` client.

```
import { fal } from "@fal-ai/client";

const connection = fal.realtime.connect("fal-ai/personaplex/realtime", {
  onResult: (result) => {
    console.log(result);
  },
  onError: (error) => {
    console.error(error);
  },
  // Fetch short-lived JWT token from your backend
  tokenProvider: async (app) => {
    const response = await fetch("/api/fal/realtime-token", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      body: JSON.stringify({ app }),
    });
    return response.text();
  },
  tokenExpirationSeconds: 10,
});

connection.send({
  audio: ""
});
```

## 2\. Authentication [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#auth)

The API uses an API Key for authentication. It is recommended you set the `FAL_KEY` environment variable in your runtime when possible.

### API Key [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#auth-api-key)

In case your app is running in an environment where you cannot set environment variables, you can set the API Key manually as a client configuration.

```
import { fal } from "@fal-ai/client";

fal.config({
  credentials: "YOUR_FAL_KEY"
});
```

##### Protect your API Key

When running code on the client-side (e.g. in a browser, mobile app or GUI applications), make sure to not expose your `FAL_KEY`. Instead, **use a server-side proxy** to make requests to the API. For more information, check out our [server-side integration guide](https://docs.fal.ai/model-endpoints/server-side).

## 4\. Files [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#files)

Some attributes in the API accept file URLs as input. Whenever that's the case you can pass your own URL or a Base64 data URI.

### Data URI (base64) [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#files-data-uri)

You can pass a Base64 data URI as a file input. The API will handle the file decoding for you. Keep in mind that for large files, this alternative although convenient can impact the request performance.

### Hosted files (URL) [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#files-from-url)

You can also pass your own URLs as long as they are publicly accessible. Be aware that some hosts might block cross-site requests, rate-limit, or consider the request as a bot.

### Uploading files [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#files-upload)

We provide a convenient file storage that allows you to upload files and use them in your requests. You can upload files using the client API and use the returned URL in your requests.

```
import { fal } from "@fal-ai/client";

const file = new File(["Hello, World!"], "hello.txt", { type: "text/plain" });
const url = await fal.storage.upload(file);
```

##### Auto uploads

The client will auto-upload the file for you if you pass a binary object (e.g. `File`, `Data`).

Read more about file handling in our [file upload guide](https://docs.fal.ai/model-endpoints#file-uploads).

## 5\. Schema [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#schema)

### Input [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#schema-input)

`voice``VoiceEnum`

Voice ID for the AI response. NAT = natural, VAR = variety. F = female, M = male. Ignored when voice\_audio\_url is provided. Default value: `"NATF2"`

Possible enum values: `NATF0, NATF1, NATF2, NATF3, NATM0, NATM1, NATM2, NATM3, VARF0, VARF1, VARF2, VARF3, VARF4, VARM0, VARM1, VARM2, VARM3, VARM4`

`temperature_text``float`

Text sampling temperature. Higher values produce more diverse outputs. Default value: `0.7`

`voice_audio_url``string`

URL to a voice sample audio for on-the-fly voice cloning. When provided, the AI responds in the cloned voice instead of the preset 'voice'. 10+ seconds of clear speech recommended. Billed at 2x rate. Default value: `"null"`

`top_k_audio``integer`

Top-K sampling for audio tokens. Default value: `250`

`seed``integer`

Random seed for reproducibility.

`temperature_audio``float`

Audio sampling temperature. Higher values produce more diverse outputs. Default value: `0.8`

`prompt``string`

Text prompt describing the AI persona and conversation context. Default value: `"You are a wise and friendly teacher. Answer questions or provide advice in a clear and engaging way."`

`audio``string`\\* required

Input audio chunk (PCM s16le, 24kHz mono). Base64-encoded in JSON transport.

`top_k_text``integer`

Top-K sampling for text tokens. Default value: `25`

```
{
  "voice": "NATF2",
  "temperature_text": 0.7,
  "top_k_audio": 250,
  "temperature_audio": 0.8,
  "prompt": "You work for SwiftPlex Appliances which is a appliance repair company and your name is Farhod Toshmatov. Information: The dishwasher model is out of stock for replacement parts; we can use an alternative part with a 3-day delay. Labor cost remains $60 per hour.",
  "audio": "",
  "top_k_text": 25
}
```

### Output [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#schema-output)

`text``string`

Generated text tokens for this chunk. Default value: `""`

`audio``string`\\* required

Generated audio chunk (PCM s16le, 24kHz mono). Base64-encoded in JSON transport.

```
{
  "audio": ""
}
```

### Other types [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#schema-other)

#### File [\#](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime/api\#type-File)

`url``string`\\* required

The URL where the file can be downloaded from.

`content_type``string`

The mime type of the file.

`file_name``string`

The name of the file. It will be auto-generated if not provided.

`file_size``integer`

The size of the file in bytes.

attachment.snippet:
1	# TSUBAKI — realtime voice console
2	
3	[![Oxc](https://github.com/jessearmand/subaki-realtime/actions/workflows/oxc.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jessearmand/subaki-realtime/actions/workflows/oxc.yml)
4	[![Build](https://github.com/jessearmand/subaki-realtime/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jessearmand/subaki-realtime/actions/workflows/build.yml)
5	[![CodeQL](https://github.com/jessearmand/subaki-realtime/actions/workflows/codeql.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jessearmand/subaki-realtime/actions/workflows/codeql.yml)
6	[![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
7	
8	A brutalist/editorial realtime voice console, recreated from a Claude Design
9	handoff and built on **ElevenLabs UI** primitives. Four screens — Sessions
10	(call), Personas, Providers, Settings — with a full call lifecycle
11	(idle → connecting → listening → speaking → interrupted → ended).
12	
13	Multi-provider by design: the UI binds to a provider-agnostic session adapter.
14	Every provider row runs the mocked lifecycle except **ElevenLabs**, which is
15	wired to a real agent via `@elevenlabs/react`.
16	
17	## Stack
18	
19	- **Next.js** (App Router) · **React 19** · **Tailwind v4**
20	- **bun** package manager · **oxlint** + **oxfmt** (lint/format)
21	- **ElevenLabs UI** (shadcn-style, copied into `components/ui/`): `Orb` (WebGL,
22	  gradient style), `BarVisualizer` (soundbars), `MicSelector` (device picker)
23	- Hybrid orb: ElevenLabs WebGL orb for `gradient`; ported CSS/SVG orb for
24	  `mono` / `particles`
25	
26	## Getting started
27	
28	```bash
29	bun install
30	bun run dev        # http://localhost:3000
31	```
32	
33	Or via **mise** tasks (load fnox secrets and give you a clean stop):
34	
35	```bash
36	mise run dev       # dev server + Mistral STT proxy (all fnox keys loaded)
37	mise run stop      # stop the server on PORT (default 3000)
38	```
39	
40	`mise run dev` also starts the realtime-STT proxy in the background (and stops it
41	with the server) so the cascade engine works out of the box — see the Cascade
42	section below.
43	
44	Other scripts:
45	
46	```bash
47	bun run lint       # oxlint
48	bun run fmt        # oxfmt (write)
49	bun run build      # production build
50	```
51	
52	## Wiring the real ElevenLabs provider
53	
54	Create `.env.local` (gitignored):
55	
56	```bash
57	# Public agent: ID is enough. Private agents need a signed-URL token route.
58	NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID=your-agent-id
59	ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=your-api-key
60	```
61	
62	Then pick the **ELEVENLABS** row under Providers and press CALL — it grants the
63	mic, streams a live transcript, and drives the orb/bars from real audio.
64	
65	## Wiring the real xAI Grok provider
66	
67	xAI's realtime API is **WebSocket-only** (no native browser WebRTC). The browser
68	connects directly to `wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime`, authenticated by a short-lived
69	**ephemeral client-secret** minted server-side at `POST /api/xai/token` — the
70	secret `XAI_API_KEY` never reaches the client.
71	
72	The only secret is the API key — keep it in **fnox** and run via
73	`fnox exec -- bun run dev`. No `XAI_*` values live in `.env` files.
74	
75	Everything declarative (model, voice, multi-line instructions, opening line,
76	tools) lives in a typed config module — **`lib/realtime/xai-agent.ts`** — the way
77	ElevenLabs keeps each agent in `agent_configs/*.json`. It's a shared `BASE`
78	(model/tools/turn-detection) plus a **per-persona** map: each app persona
79	(`ARIA`/`ONYX`/`SAGE`/`NOVA`/`ECHO`/`CIPHER`) maps to a Grok voice + its own
80	prompt + greeting. The selected persona drives the live session via
81	`resolveXaiAgent(personaId)`. Edit that file to personalize — no env strings.
82	
83	Pick the **XAI** row under Providers (it's the default), choose a persona, and
84	press CALL — it mints a token, opens the WebSocket, captures the mic as PCM16,
85	plays the agent's audio, streams transcripts, and barges in on server-VAD speech
86	detection. Without `XAI_API_KEY` set, CALL shows a clear "XAI_API_KEY is not set"
87	caption instead of connecting.
88	
89	## Wiring the real OpenAI provider
90	
91	OpenAI's realtime API (`gpt-realtime-2`) connects over **WebRTC** — the browser's
92	peer connection carries the audio both ways, so there's no hand-rolled PCM
93	pipeline. A short-lived **ephemeral key** is minted server-side at
94	`POST /api/openai/token`; the browser then POSTs its SDP offer straight to
95	`https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls` with that key, and session control +
96	transcripts flow over the `oai-events` data channel. The secret `OPENAI_API_KEY`
97	never reaches the client.
98	
99	Keep `OPENAI_API_KEY` in **fnox** and run via `fnox exec -- bun run dev`. No
100	`OPENAI_*` values live in `.env` files.
101	
102	Per-persona config (voice, multi-line instructions, opening line, reasoning
103	effort, turn-detection) lives in the typed module **`lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts`**
104	— a shared `BASE` (model / reasoning / `gpt-realtime-whisper` input transcription /
105	turn-detection) plus a per-persona map of OpenAI voice + prompt + greeting,
106	resolved by `resolveOpenaiAgent(personaId)`. The persona `instructions` follow a
107	light slice of OpenAI's Realtime 2.0 prompt skeleton (Role, Personality & Tone,
108	Pacing, Unclear Audio, Variety).
109	
110	Pick the **OPENAI** row under Providers, choose a persona, and press CALL — it
111	mints a key, negotiates WebRTC, plays the agent's audio, shows the user + agent
112	transcripts (whisper for input), and barges in on server-VAD speech detection.
113	Without `OPENAI_API_KEY` set, CALL shows a clear "OPENAI_API_KEY is not set"
114	caption instead of connecting.
115	
116	## Wiring the fal.ai PersonaPlex provider (full-duplex)
117	
118	The **FAL.AI** row runs [NVIDIA PersonaPlex](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1)
119	hosted on fal.ai ([`fal-ai/personaplex/realtime`](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime))
120	— a **full-duplex** speech-to-speech model that listens while it speaks. Unlike
121	every other engine there is no VAD and no turn events: the model opens the call
122	with its own greeting, barge-in is native (just talk over it), and INTERRUPT is
123	effectively a no-op. There is no user-side transcript (no ASR in the path); the
124	agent transcript streams from the model's inner-monologue text tokens.
125	
126	Transport is a direct browser→fal WebSocket

1	# PersonaPlex local inference on Apple Silicon (MLX)
2	
3	Status: **Phase 1 verified on hardware** — q8 is realtime on M5 Max (benchmarks below); live web server runs at `localhost:8998`. Remaining: subjective live-conversation notes (requires mic + headphones — the bundled client has no echo cancellation).
4	
5	## What we're running
6	
7	- **Model:** [nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1) — full-duplex speech-to-speech (Moshi architecture, 8.37B params incl. depth transformer + Mimi codec), conditioned on a voice prompt (`NATF0-3`, `NATM0-3`, `VARF0-4`, `VARM0-4` presets) and a free-text persona prompt. Gated: auto-approve after accepting the NVIDIA Open Model License (account-level, do it once in the browser).
8	- **Runtime:** [mu-hashmi/personaplex-mlx](https://github.com/mu-hashmi/personaplex-mlx) — Python MLX port (moshi_mlx fork) with realtime web mode (`personaplex_mlx.local_web`), realtime terminal mode, and offline WAV mode. Quantizes the bf16 checkpoint at load time (`-q 4|8`).
9	- **Follow-up checkpoint (Phase 2):** [kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless) — RL fine-tune for turn-taking/backchanneling. Gated, bf16 only, RL delta licensed CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial).
10	
11	## Setup (commands that worked)
12	
13	```bash
14	git clone https://github.com/mu-hashmi/personaplex-mlx ~/Develop/personaplex-mlx
15	cd ~/Develop/personaplex-mlx
16	uv venv --python 3.12 .venv
17	uv pip install -e . --python .venv/bin/python
18	
19	# one-time: accept the license at https://huggingface.co/nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1
20	hf download nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1   # ~17GB model.safetensors + tokenizer + mimi + voices.tgz + dist.tgz
21	
22	.venv/bin/python -m personaplex_mlx.local_web -q 8 \
23	  --voice NATF2 \
24	  --text-prompt "You enjoy having a good conversation."
25	# web client + WebSocket at http://localhost:8998
26	```
27	
28	Notes:
29	
30	- `-q 8` quantizes in-process from bf16 (no pre-quantized `model.q8.safetensors` exists in the NVIDIA repo). Community benchmarks of the Swift MLX build report 4-bit produces garbled output; prefer 8-bit or bf16.
31	- The bundled web client has **no echo cancellation** — use headphones.
32	- Quantization at load is cheap (~2s total to load + quantize on M5 Max), so there's no need to persist quantized weights.
33	- Benchmark harness: `bench_steps.py` in the fork checkout (`~/Develop/personaplex-mlx`); response audio samples: `bench-output-q8.wav` / `bench-output-bf16.wav` there.
34	
35	## Phase 2: kyutai RL checkpoint (done — 2026-06-18)
36	
37	`kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless` is gated **auto** and its file layout is identical to base (`model.safetensors`, same Mimi checkpoint, tokenizer, `voices.tgz` — same 18 NATF/NATM/VARF/VARM voices). License accepted on account jessearmand. Runs via the same server:
38	
39	```bash
40	.venv/bin/python -m personaplex_mlx.local_web -q 8 --hf-repo kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless ...
41	```
42	
43	**One code fix was required.** Unlike base (whose `config.json` is a stub with no `dim`, routing to the hardcoded `config_personaplex_7b_v1()`), the RL repo ships a *full* `config.json`, so the fork parses it via `LmConfig.from_config_dict` — which had two bugs: it hardcoded the feed-forward width as `4 * dim` (PersonaPlex uses `hidden_scale = 4.125`, so weights wouldn't match) and passed `depformer_dim_feedforward` straight through (it's `null` in the RL config → `TypeError`). Fixed `from_config_dict` in `personaplex_mlx/models/lm.py` to honor `hidden_scale` (default 4) for both the main and depformer feed-forward dims. After the fix the RL model loads and runs realtime at q8: **67.3 ms/step mean, p95 70.2 ms, RTF 0.84, 10.1 GB** (≈3 ms/step slower than base, still comfortably realtime).
44	
45	### A/B vs base — greeting cadence is unchanged
46	
47	RL-seamless is RL-tuned for **interaction dynamics** (pause handling, turn-taking, backchanneling, user interruption), *not* solo-monologue fluency. Confirmed by an opening-greeting cadence A/B (voiced fraction of the first 3 s, silence mic, 3 seeds each via `scratchpad/cadence.py`):
48	
49	| model | medical greeting (voiced %, 3 seeds) |
50	| ----- | ------------------------------------ |
51	| base `nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1` | 63 / 56 / 75 (avg ~65%) |
52	| RL `kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless` | 68 / 64 / 62 (avg ~65%) |
53	
54	Statistically identical — **RL does not fix the halting/choppy opening greeting** (that cadence is inherent to the architecture's solo speech rhythm, and is already faithfully reproduced; see the residual-glitch section). RL's benefit appears only in live conversation (turn-taking, fewer mid-greeting/mid-turn self-interruptions), which the headless silence probes can't exercise — evaluate it in the browser. The mic-gate already covers the greeting-interruption case for both checkpoints.
55	
56	A user recording of a full RL conversation (`astronaut_conversation.webm`, 5m39s) confirms it: onset 0.29s but only ~1% voiced in the first 3s — the opening is tiny fragments (70–360ms) then a 3.6s wait, **zero clicks** (max sample step 0.103). Same halting cadence as base, no codec artifact.
57	
58	### Why the halting cadence is inherent to the architecture
59	
60	The "glitch" is the model's *speaking rhythm*, and it falls out of how Moshi/PersonaPlex generates — it is not a bug we can tune away in the serving stack:
61	
62	1. **Frame-synchronous streaming at 12.5 Hz with an "inner monologue."** Every 80 ms the model jointly samples **one text token** — an inner-monologue word-piece, *or* a `PAD`/`EPAD` token (ids 0–3) meaning "emit no word this frame" — together with the matching Mimi audio codebooks (`delays=[0,0,1,1,…]` is the text→audio acoustic offset). Speech only comes out on frames where the text stream emits a real word-piece; between word-pieces it emits `PAD` and the audio is silence/breath. So speech is *intrinsically* delivered in word/syllable-sized bursts separated by pad-driven gaps — **the 50–360 ms "gaps" we measure are `PAD` runs in the inner monologue, not dropped audio.**
63	
64	2. **No utterance-level prosody planning.** To stay ready to yield to the user at any 80 ms frame (full-duplex), the model commits token-by-token with no look-ahead over the whole sentence. A non-streaming TTS plans a smooth pitch/timing contour across the entire utterance; Moshi decides "speak or pad" and "which word-piece" one frame at a time under temperature sampling. That yields choppier, less-planned timing — most pronounced at turn onset, before the model "gets going."
65	
66	3. **Trained on natural two-person dialogue.** The data is real conversational speech — hesitations, variable pacing, mid-sentence pauses — not the polished read-aloud prosody of TTS corpora. The model faithfully reproduces that disfluent, conversational cadence rather than narration smoothness.
67	
68	4. **It's the price of full-duplex.** The very mechanism that lets the model listen and barge-in at 80 ms granularity (per-frame speak/pad decision, no look-ahead) is what makes its monologue halting. One autoregressive stream can't be both narration-smooth *and* 80 ms-responsive. RL-seamless tunes *when* to pad/yield in response to the user (turn-taking); the *within-turn* word-by-word delivery is structural — hence unchanged in the A/B above.
69	
70	**Implication:** smoothing the opening would require a different model class (a non-streaming TTS for the greeting, or a half-duplex turn-based model that plans whole utterances), not a fix to PersonaPlex serving. Within PersonaPlex the levers are marginal — lower audio-sampling temperature, voice-prompt choice, or simply accepting it as the model's conversational voice. This is the main reason to evaluate alternatives like the Voxtral cascade ([voxtral-local-inference.md](voxtral-local-inference.md)).

10	This project is **Tsubaki** (renamed from **Persona·Plex** — 古椿の霊, the old-camellia-tree spirit; default accent is camellia crimson `#B0122F`, burnt orange still selectable), a brutalist/editorial multi-provider realtime voice console recreated from a Claude Design handoff bundle, built on Next.js (App Router) + bun + oxlint/oxfmt, using ElevenLabs UI primitives (`Orb`, `BarVisualizer`, `MicSelector`). The full internal rename landed: `components/tsubaki/`, CSS scope `.tsubaki`/`.tsubaki-dark`, var prefix `--tb-`, class prefix `tb-`.
11	
12	Key architectural intent:
13	- The UI binds to a provider-agnostic `SessionApi` (`lib/realtime/`). `provider.engine` selects the engine: absent ⇒ **mock** lifecycle; `elevenlabs` ⇒ `@elevenlabs/react` `useConversation` + `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID`; `xai` ⇒ direct WebSocket (`use-xai-session` + `xai-audio` PCM16 + `/api/xai/token`); `openai` ⇒ **gpt-realtime-2 over WebRTC** (`use-openai-session` + `/api/openai/token`, ephemeral key → `POST /v1/realtime/calls`; WebRTC handles all audio, no PCM pipeline; input transcript via `gpt-realtime-whisper`). The two custom hooks share one interface; `use-realtime-session` picks the active one as `custom` and routes all controls through it.
14	- Per-persona config lives in typed modules: `lib/realtime/xai-agent.ts` (`resolveXaiAgent`) and `lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts` (`resolveOpenaiAgent`, OpenAI voices + `reasoningEffort` + light Realtime 2.0 prompt skeleton). OpenAI turn detection uses **`semantic_vad`** (eagerness `low` for slow personas, `medium` for snappy) after the user found energy-based `server_vad` too sensitive to room noise; the `turnDetection` type also still supports `server_vad` (threshold/silence/prefix) + `create_response`/`interrupt_response`. Verified: OpenAI accepts the semantic_vad payload (no error) and speech_started fires far less often.
15	- Hybrid orb: ElevenLabs WebGL orb for the `gradient` style; ported CSS/SVG orb for `mono`/`particles`. OpenAI orb levels come from Web Audio `AnalyserNode`s tapping the mic + remote WebRTC streams.
16	
17	**Real provider status:** ElevenLabs **VERIFIED working end-to-end** — live session against the user's public `explorer` agent (connect → token 200 → LiveKit WebRTC → live STT/TTS + orb → hang-up). xAI Grok integration landed (on `main`). OpenAI `gpt-realtime-2` (WebRTC) integration landed on branch `feat/gpt-voice-agent` and is **VERIFIED working end-to-end** in Chrome (chrome-devtools MCP): `/api/openai/token` 200 → `POST /v1/realtime/calls` 201 → data channel → `session.update` applied the persona voice+instructions (ARIA greeted warmly in-character) → agent transcript streamed into caption + drawer turns → barge-in/VAD events + user-input whisper transcription events flow → clean hang-up teardown. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is now in fnox. Mock also fully verified.
18	
19	Fixes/learnings from wiring it (all in `lib/realtime/use-realtime-session.ts`):
20	- `@elevenlabs/react` `useConversation` methods (`setMuted`, `getInputVolume`, `getOutputVolume`) **throw "No active conversation" if called before `startSession()`**. The mute effect was crashing the page the moment ELEVENLABS was selected. Guard `setMuted` on `status === "connected"`; wrap the volume getters in try/catch → return 0. The mock being the default provider is why this stayed latent.
21	- `livekit-client` is pinned to `2.16.1` via `package.json` `overrides` (skill-recommended WebRTC workaround); it already resolved there anyway.
22	- Agent IDs are **not secret** (public-widget embeddable). The user's key lives in **fnox**; for non-interactive shells use `fnox exec -- <cmd>` (the `fnox activate` zsh hook doesn't fire). `.env*` writes are blocked by a hook, so for a quick dev test export inline: `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID=<id> bun run dev` (persist via `.env.local` yourself).
23	- List the user's agents: `fnox exec -- elevenlabs agents list`. All three (explorer / Travel guide / Japan Culture Expert) are `enable_auth:false` → connectable with agent ID alone, no signed-URL route.
24	
25	**How to apply:** consult [[elevenlabs-skills]] (`agents` + `setup-api-key`) before changing the integration.

content.text:
The engine is now **verified working end-to-end against the live fal.ai endpoint** — and the test caught a real protocol bug that I fixed along the way.

**Review of your changes:** the `FAL_API_KEY` rename is consistent everywhere — [route.ts](app/api/fal/token/route.ts) reads it, fnox has it as a provider-backed secret, README and docs match, and no stale `FAL_KEY` references remain anywhere.

**The bug the test found:** with the key in place, the token minted fine (real JWT), the WebSocket connected — and then nothing came back. A headless probe showed the server **silently ignores JSON text frames**; despite the schema saying "Base64-encoded in JSON transport", the app only speaks **msgpack binary frames**, and audio travels as **raw PCM16 bytes**, not base64. Re-probing with msgpack got an immediate greeting, and a third probe streaming real speech (our bench WAV asking about travel spots) confirmed the model genuinely hears input — it answered "one of my favorite spots is Shimane Prefecture."

**Fixes applied:**
- Added `@msgpack/msgpack` (the engine's one dependency) and switched [use-fal-session.ts](lib/realtime/use-fal-session.ts) to msgpack encode/decode with raw-byte audio both ways.
- Added generic `float32ToPcm16Bytes` / `pcm16BytesToFloat32` helpers to [xai-audio.ts](lib/realtime/xai-audio.ts) (the base64 variant now reuses them).
- Corrected the README transport paragraph.

**Browser test result:** with a synthetic mic injected (the pane blocks real capture), CALL → session live via FAL.AI → PersonaPlex greeted **in persona**: *"Hello, you're calling Tsubaki. This is Aria. How can I help you?"* — transcript turn recorded, state machine behaved (LISTENING after the greeting decayed), clean hangup with WS close 1000. All gates pass and the dev server is still running.

What's left needs your ears: a real call in Chrome with headphones — actual mic, audible playback, barge-in feel, and whether the greeting gate holds up against real room noise. Then we're set up for the comparison you wanted: same persona/voice/seed on fal versus the local MLX server (with the PR #4 fix) to separate model-intrinsic cadence from serving effects.

content.text: The local server is indeed the stronger path — and it's the one where we control the whole stack (greeting gate, pacing, and the PR #4 fix are all already in your fork). The doc's integration sketch calls for one new piece: the browser side of the audio transport, and there's a real fork in the road there worth deciding deliberately.

questions.question: How should the browser talk audio to the local personaplex-mlx server? The server's native protocol is Ogg Opus over WebSocket (tag-prefixed binary frames). We own the fork, so we could instead add a PCM16 mode to local_web.py.

options.label: PCM mode in our fork (Recommended)
options.description: Add `?format=pcm` to local_web.py: raw PCM16@24kHz both ways. Browser engine then mirrors the fal engine almost verbatim (no WASM codecs, symmetric A/B with fal). ~48KB/s per direction — trivial on localhost. Diverges our fork's server slightly (bundled client keeps working via the default opus path).

options.label: Browser Opus (upstream protocol)
options.description: Use opus-recorder (encode) + ogg-opus-decoder (WASM, decode) in the browser, matching the server's existing protocol. Server untouched and upstream-compatible, but two WASM workers to integrate into Next.js and opus-recorder is unmaintained.

questions.question: Which checkpoint should the local engine target by default? (Both run via the same server; it's whatever you launch local_web with.)

options.label: kyutai RL-seamless (Recommended)
options.description: The RL fine-tune for turn-taking/backchanneling — the point of this comparison. Non-commercial license (CC BY-NC RL delta), q8 RTF 0.84. Provider row reads KYUTAI · personaplex-rl.

options.label: NVIDIA base 7b-v1
options.description: The base checkpoint (q8 RTF 0.80). Slightly faster, permissive license. RL can still be launched manually anytime.

## kyutai-personaplex-rl
 M README.md
 M bun.lock
 M docs/personaplex-local-inference.md
 M fnox.toml
 M lib/data.ts
 M lib/realtime/use-realtime-session.ts
 M lib/realtime/xai-audio.ts
 M package.json
?? app/api/fal/
?? lib/realtime/fal-agent.ts
?? lib/realtime/greeting-gate.ts
?? lib/realtime/use-fal-session.ts
[env]
NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID = "agent_0701ksfnj6kzfg2rq4gznfpjmfx4"

# ── Tasks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Secrets (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY) live in
# fnox; `fnox exec -- …` injects them for the wrapped command (the recommended
# fnox + mise pattern). Run with `mise run dev` / `mise run stop`.
# The cascade engine's realtime STT also needs `mise run stt-proxy` (separate process).

[tasks.dev]
description = "Start the Next.js dev server (+ Mistral STT proxy) with fnox secrets loaded"
run = '''
# Start the realtime-STT proxy in the background so the cascade engine has it
# without a second terminal; tear it down when the dev server exits. Without it,
# pressing CALL on the MISTRAL provider logs a harmless but noisy
# ws://localhost:3001 ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED (STT then falls back to Web Speech).
fnox exec -- bun run scripts/mistral-stt-proxy.ts &
proxy_pid=$!
trap 'kill "$proxy_pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM
fnox exec -- bun run dev
'''

[tasks.stt-proxy]
description = "Mistral realtime-STT WebSocket proxy (adds the Bearer header the browser can't); :3001"
run = "fnox exec -- bun run scripts/mistral-stt-proxy.ts"

[tasks.stop-stt-proxy]
description = "Stop the STT proxy listening on STT_PROXY_PORT (default 3001)"
run = '''
port="${STT_PROXY_PORT:-3001}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped STT proxy on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No STT proxy running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.lm-local]
description = "Serve the local cascade LM (llama-server, gemma-4-12B QAT + MTP draft); :8001"
run = '''
# Local LM leg of the cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md). Keyless —
# config/lm-models.json's `local` backend points at this server, and --alias must
# match that entry's `model` id. MTP speculative decoding via the draft head;
# text-only (no --mmproj) and thinking off, per ~/Develop/voice-cascade/README.md.
model_dir="${LM_LOCAL_MODEL_DIR:-$HOME/Develop/voice-cascade/models/gemma-4-12B}"
llama-server \
  --model "$model_dir/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf" \
  --model-draft "$model_dir/mtp-gemma-4-12B-it.gguf" \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 \
  -ngl 999 -fa on --jinja \
  --port "${LM_LOCAL_PORT:-8001}" \
  --alias unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-qat-GGUF
'''

[tasks.local-stack]
description = "Serve the full local cascade stack: LM llama-server (:8001) + mlx-audio TTS/STT (:8002)"
run = '''
# One terminal for the whole on-device cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md).
# mlx-audio runs in the background, llama-server in the foreground; Ctrl-C (or
# the foreground server dying) tears both down via the trap.
mise run audio-local &
audio_pid=$!
trap 'kill "$audio_pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM
mise run lm-local
'''

[tasks.stop-local-stack]
description = "Stop both local inference servers (:8001 + :8002)"
run = '''
mise run stop-lm-local
mise run stop-audio-local
'''

[tasks.audio-local]
description = "Serve the local TTS + batch-STT legs (mlx-audio server, Voxtral); :8002"
run = '''
# Local voice legs of the cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md). Keyless —
# config/voice-models.json's `local` tts/stt backends point here. Models load
# lazily on first request (TTS ~4 GB + STT ~3 GB resident thereafter).
audio_dir="${MLX_AUDIO_DIR:-$HOME/Develop/mlx-audio}"
cd "$audio_dir" && .venv/bin/python -m mlx_audio.server --port "${AUDIO_LOCAL_PORT:-8002}"
'''

[tasks.stop-audio-local]
description = "Stop the mlx-audio server listening on AUDIO_LOCAL_PORT (default 8002)"
run = '''
port="${AUDIO_LOCAL_PORT:-8002}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped mlx-audio server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No mlx-audio server running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.stop-lm-local]
description = "Stop the local LM server listening on LM_LOCAL_PORT (default 8001)"
run = '''
port="${LM_LOCAL_PORT:-8001}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped local LM server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No local LM server running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.stop]
description = "Stop the dev server listening on PORT (default 3000)"
run = '''
port="${PORT:-3000}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped dev server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No dev server running on :$port"
fi
'''

124	    async def handle_chat(self, request):
125	        ws = web.WebSocketResponse()
126	        await ws.prepare(request)
127	
128	        voice_name = request.query.get("voice_prompt", "")
129	        text_prompt = request.query.get("text_prompt", "")
130	        seed = int(request.query.get("seed", self.args.seed))
131	        if voice_name == "":
132	            voice_name = self.args.voice_prompt or self.args.voice
133	        if text_prompt == "":
134	            text_prompt = self.args.text_prompt
135	
136	        voice_path = resolve_voice_prompt(
137	            voice=None,
138	            voice_prompt=voice_name,
139	            voice_prompt_dir=self.args.voice_prompt_dir,
140	        )
141	
142	        input_queue: queue.Queue[np.ndarray] = queue.Queue()
143	        text_queue: queue.Queue[str] = queue.Queue()
144	        audio_tokenizer = rustymimi.StreamTokenizer(self.mimi_file, num_codebooks=8)  # type: ignore
145	        opus_writer = sphn.OpusStreamWriter(SAMPLE_RATE)
146	        opus_reader = sphn.OpusStreamReader(SAMPLE_RATE)
147	        output_pacer = OutboundAudioPacer(SAMPLE_RATE)
148	        greeting_gate = (
149	            GreetingGate(
150	                SAMPLE_RATE,
151	                voice_rms=self.args.greeting_gate_rms,
152	                end_silence_s=self.args.greeting_gate_end_ms / 1000,
153	                max_s=self.args.greeting_gate_max_ms / 1000,
154	            )
155	            if self.args.greeting_gate
156	            else None
157	        )
158	        close = False
159	
160	        async def recv_loop():
161	            nonlocal close
162	            all_pcm_data = None
163	            try:
164	                async for message in ws:
165	                    if message.type in (
166	                        aiohttp.WSMsgType.ERROR,
167	                        aiohttp.WSMsgType.CLOSE,
168	                        aiohttp.WSMsgType.CLOSED,
169	                    ):
170	                        break
171	                    if message.type != aiohttp.WSMsgType.BINARY:
172	                        continue
173	                    payload = message.data
174	                    if not isinstance(payload, bytes) or len(payload) == 0:
175	                        continue
176	                    if payload[0] != 1:
177	                        continue
178	                    pcm = opus_reader.append_bytes(payload[1:])
179	                    if pcm.shape[-1] == 0:
180	                        continue
181	                    if all_pcm_data is None:
182	                        all_pcm_data = pcm
183	                    else:
184	                        all_pcm_data = np.concatenate((all_pcm_data, pcm))
185	                    while all_pcm_data.shape[-1] >= FRAME_SIZE:
186	                        chunk = all_pcm_data[:FRAME_SIZE]
187	                        all_pcm_data = all_pcm_data[FRAME_SIZE:]
188	                        # Mic-gate the opening greeting: feed the model silence
189	                        # until it finishes greeting, so it doesn't yield its turn
190	                        # on ambient mic noise and chop its own greeting.
191	                        if greeting_gate is not None and greeting_gate.is_muted():
192	                            input_queue.put_nowait(np.zeros(FRAME_SIZE, dtype=np.float32))
193	                        else:
194	                            input_queue.put_nowait(chunk.astype(np.float32))
195	            finally:
196	                close = True
197	
198	        async def encode_loop():
199	            while True:
200	                if close:
201	                    return
202	                await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
203	                try:
204	                    pcm = input_queue.get(block=False)
205	                except queue.Empty:
206	                    continue
207	                audio_tokenizer.encode(pcm)
208	
209	        async def model_loop():
210	            while True:
211	                if close:
212	                    return
213	                tokens = audio_tokenizer.get_encoded()
214	                if tokens is None:
215	                    await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
216	                    continue
217	                model_input = mx.array(tokens).transpose(1, 0)[:, : self.gen.user_codebooks]
218	                model_input = model_input[:, :, None]
219	                text_token = REDACTED
220	                if text_token is not None:
221	                    text_value = int(text_token[0].item())
222	                    if text_value not in (0, 3):
223	                        piece = self.text_tokenizer.id_to_piece(text_value)  # type: ignore
224	                        text_queue.put_nowait(piece.replace("▁", " "))
225	                audio_tokens = self.gen.last_audio_tokens()
226	                if audio_tokens is not None:
227	                    audio_tokenizer.decode(np.array(audio_tokens).astype(np.uint32))
228	                # Yield between steps so send_loop can pace/flush output. Without
229	                # this, a startup backlog of encoded frames is consumed in a tight
230	                # run of ~64ms blocking MLX steps, starving send_loop for ~0.5s and
231	                # underrunning the browser jitter buffer (greeting crackle).
232	                await asyncio.sleep(0)
233	
234	        async def send_loop():
235	            nonlocal close
236	            while True:
237	                if close:
238	                    return
239	                await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
240	                if ws.closed:
241	                    close = True
242	                    return
243	                decoded = audio_tokenizer.get_decoded()

import numpy as np

from personaplex_mlx.local_web import float_to_pcm16_bytes, pcm16_bytes_to_float


def test_roundtrip_preserves_signal():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    pcm = rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0, size=1920).astype(np.float32)
    out = pcm16_bytes_to_float(float_to_pcm16_bytes(pcm))
    assert out.shape == pcm.shape
    assert out.dtype == np.float32
    assert np.max(np.abs(out - pcm)) < 1.0 / 32000


def test_encode_clips_out_of_range():
    pcm = np.array([-2.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0], dtype=np.float32)
    out = pcm16_bytes_to_float(float_to_pcm16_bytes(pcm))
    assert np.all(out >= -1.0) and np.all(out <= 1.0)
    assert out[0] == out[1]  # clipped to the same extreme
    assert out[3] == out[4]


def test_decode_drops_trailing_odd_byte():
    raw = float_to_pcm16_bytes(np.zeros(4, dtype=np.float32)) + b"\x7f"
    assert pcm16_bytes_to_float(raw).shape == (4,)


def test_decode_empty_and_single_byte():
    assert pcm16_bytes_to_float(b"").shape == (0,)
    assert pcm16_bytes_to_float(b"\x00").shape == (0,)

## WebSocket protocol (`/api/chat`)

Binary frames; the first byte is a tag: `0x00` handshake (server → client, once
the prompts are stepped), `0x01` audio, `0x02` agent text token (UTF-8). Session

`text_prompt`, `seed`, and `format`:

  (24 kHz mono) in both directions. This is what the bundled web client speaks.
- `format=pcm` — `0x01` frames carry **raw PCM16 little-endian @ 24 kHz** in
  both directions. No codec needed; intended for external clients on localhost
  (e.g. a browser app with a 24 kHz `AudioContext`). ~48 KB/s per direction.

The model steps are input-driven: a client must stream mic frames continuously
(silence included — e.g. while muted) or generation stalls.

# PersonaPlex-MLX

MLX inference for NVIDIA PersonaPlex on Apple Silicon.

This package supports:

- Realtime local mode (`personaplex_mlx.local`)
- Realtime web mode (`personaplex_mlx.local_web`)
- Offline WAV-to-WAV mode (`personaplex_mlx.offline`)

Console entrypoints are also installed: `personaplex-local`, `personaplex-local-web`, `personaplex-offline`.

## Requirements

- Apple Silicon Mac
- Python 3.12
- Hugging Face access to `nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1`

Install (uv, recommended):

```bash
uv sync            # runtime deps
uv sync --extra dev  # + ruff, ty, pytest, pre-commit
```

Or with pip:

```bash
pip install -e .
```

## Model Access

Accept the model license:
`https://huggingface.co/nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1`

Set your token:

```bash
export HF_TOKEN=<your_token>
```

## Quickstart

Launch realtime web mode (recommended first):

```bash
python -m personaplex_mlx.local_web \
  -q 8 \
  --voice NATF2 \
  --text-prompt "You enjoy having a good conversation."
```

Open `http://localhost:8998` in your browser.

Realtime local terminal mode:

```bash
python -m personaplex_mlx.local \
  -q 8 \
  --voice NATF2 \
  --text-prompt "You enjoy having a good conversation."
```

Quantization: `-q 8` stays realtime with headroom on Apple Silicon (M5 Max:
64 ms/step mean vs the 80 ms frame budget) while bf16 is borderline and 4-bit
degrades output quality. Weights are quantized in-process at load (~2 s), so
nothing is persisted.

Offline inference:

```bash
python -m personaplex_mlx.offline \
  --voice NATF2 \
  --text-prompt "You are a wise and friendly teacher. Answer questions or provide advice in a clear and engaging way." \
  --input-wav input.wav \
  --output-wav output.wav \
  --output-text output.json \
  --seed 42424242
```

## Alternate checkpoint: kyutai RL fine-tune

[`kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless`](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless)
(RL-tuned for turn-taking and backchanneling; gated, RL delta licensed
CC BY-NC 4.0) runs via the same server — accept its license first, then:

```bash
python -m personaplex_mlx.local_web \
  -q 8 \
  --hf-repo kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless \
  --voice NATF2 \
  --text-prompt "You enjoy having a good conversation."
```

It ships the same Mimi checkpoint, tokenizer, and voice presets as the base
model. Its full `config.json` is parsed directly (honoring `hidden_scale`),
unlike the base repo's stub config which routes to the hardcoded 7B config.

## Greeting stability

The opening greeting is sensitive to serving hiccups; three fixes keep it clean:

- **Realtime output pacing** — decoded PCM is released at realtime cadence
  instead of bursting ahead of the browser client's small jitter buffer.
- **Startup warmup + per-session graph sync** — sampling kernels are compiled
  once at server startup, and each session's voice/system-prompt graph is
  force-evaluated *before* the client handshake, so the model steps in
  steady-state time from the first mic frame.
- **Greeting gate** (on by default) — the model hears silence until it has
  finished its opening greeting, so ambient mic noise (or AGC-boosted room
  tone) can't make the full-duplex model interrupt its own greeting. Tune or
  disable with:

```
--no-greeting-gate            disable the gate
--greeting-gate-rms 0.02      output RMS that counts as voiced
--greeting-gate-end-ms 600    trailing quiet that ends the greeting turn
--greeting-gate-max-ms 12000  safety cap before the gate opens regardless
```

## Development

```bash
uv sync --extra dev
uv run pytest tests/ -q
uv run ruff check personaplex_mlx/
uv run ty check personaplex_mlx/
```

`scratchpad/` holds diagnostic probes (greeting timing, cadence, gate E2E) and
temporary audio artifacts; it is not part of the package.

## Voices

Built-in voice IDs:

- `NATF0` `NATF1` `NATF2` `NATF3`
- `NATM0` `NATM1` `NATM2` `NATM3`
- `VARF0` `VARF1` `VARF2` `VARF3` `VARF4`
- `VARM0` `VARM1` `VARM2` `VARM3` `VARM4`

`--voice NATF2` resolves to `NATF2.pt` from the downloaded `voices/` bundle.

## Notes

- First run downloads model assets from Hugging Face.
- Local and web clients are barebone and do not include echo cancellation. Use headphones to avoid feedback.

## Attribution

This project is an MLX port of NVIDIA PersonaPlex for Apple Silicon.

- NVIDIA PersonaPlex repo: `https://github.com/NVIDIA/personaplex`
- PersonaPlex model card: `https://huggingface.co/nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1`

## Citation

If you use PersonaPlex in research, cite:

```bibtex

  title={PersonaPlex: Voice and Role Control for Full Duplex Conversational Speech Models},
  author={Rajarshi Roy and Jonathan Raiman and Sang-gil Lee and Teodor-Dumitru Ene and Robert Kirby and Sungwon Kim and Jaehyeon Kim and Bryan Catanzaro},
  year={2026},

Two full-duplex quirks are handled in `lib/realtime/use-fal-session.ts`:

- **Greeting gate** (`lib/realtime/greeting-gate.ts`): the mic is replaced with
  silence until the model finishes its opening greeting, and `autoGainControl`
  is off — otherwise amplified room tone makes the model interrupt its own
  greeting mid-sentence. (Same logic we validated server-side in the local MLX
  fork; see `docs/personaplex-local-inference.md`.)
- **Continuous timeline**: mute and the gate send silence chunks instead of
  pausing sends — the model tracks the conversation as two synchronized audio
  streams, so the input clock must never stop.

Use headphones — the model hears everything the mic hears, including its own
voice from speakers. Pick the **FAL.AI** row under Providers, choose a persona,
and press CALL. Without `FAL_API_KEY` set, CALL shows a clear "FAL_API_KEY is not set"
caption instead of connecting.

## Wiring the Cascade provider (STT → LM → TTS)

The **MISTRAL** row runs a turn-based cascade instead of a single full-duplex
model: **Mistral realtime STT** → **`/api/llm`** (LM) → **`/api/mistral/tts`**
(Voxtral TTS). Per-persona prompt/voice live in `lib/realtime/cascade-agent.ts`
(voices are Mistral slugs like `en_paul_neutral`); the **LM model is configured
separately** (see below):

## Wiring the local KYUTAI provider (full-duplex, on-device)

The **KYUTAI** row runs the same PersonaPlex architecture fully **on-device**:
the [kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless](https://huggingface.co/kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless)
RL fine-tune (better turn-taking/backchanneling; non-commercial RL delta) served
by our [personaplex-mlx fork](https://github.com/jessearmand/personaplex-mlx)
(`tsubaki-server` branch) at q8 on Apple Silicon. Start the server, then the app:

```bash
mise run personaplex-local   # personaplex-mlx local_web on :8998 (kyutai RL, q8)
mise run dev
```

`PERSONAPLEX_HF_REPO=nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1 mise run personaplex-local` serves
the base checkpoint instead; `PERSONAPLEX_DIR`/`PERSONAPLEX_PORT` override the
checkout path (default `~/Develop/personaplex-mlx`) and port. No API key — the
browser connects straight to `ws://localhost:8998/api/chat` with the persona's
`voice_prompt`/`text_prompt` as query params and **`format=pcm`**, our fork's
codec-free wire mode (raw PCM16 @ 24 kHz in the tag-prefixed binary frames; see
the fork's README for the protocol).

Engine: `lib/realtime/use-moshi-session.ts`. Persona conditioning (voice preset
+ role prompt) is **shared with the fal engine** via
`lib/realtime/personaplex-personas.ts`, so an A/B between KYUTAI and FAL.AI
varies only the serving stack. Differences from the fal engine: no token route,
and the greeting mic-gate runs **server-side** (our fork has it on by default)
instead of in the browser. Everything else matches — model greets first,
barge-in is native, mute streams silence (the local model's steps are
input-driven, so the mic clock must never stop), headphones recommended.

## Tsubaki integration — full-duplex `moshi` engine (assessed, not yet built)

No WebRTC and no new web architecture needed — this is a direct-WebSocket engine like xAI (`lib/realtime/use-xai-session.ts`):

- `use-moshi-session.ts` implementing `SessionApi`; provider entry `engine: "moshi"` → `ws://localhost:8998/api/chat`; per-persona `moshi-agent.ts` resolving voice/text prompts into query params.
- New piece: browser-side Opus (`opus-recorder` encode / `ogg-opus-decoder` decode) instead of PCM16-base64; playback reuses `PlaybackQueue` from `xai-audio.ts`.
- Full-duplex consequences: no user-side transcript (no ASR events), `interrupt()` is a no-op (model handles barge-in natively), `callState` derives from output audio activity.
- **Mic-gate the opening greeting** (see residual-glitch section): hold/threshold mic frames until the greeting completes, and set `autoGainControl:false` (keep `echoCancellation`/`noiseSuppression`), so ambient noise doesn't make the model interrupt its own greeting.

## Tsubaki integration — full-duplex `moshi` engine (BUILT — 2026-07-13)

Landed as the **KYUTAI** provider row (`engine: "moshi"`), verified live in-browser against the RL checkpoint (Aria greeted in-character, then followed up on its own — the RL model's backchannel behavior). As assessed: a direct-WebSocket engine like xAI, with one deviation from the original plan — **no browser Opus**. Instead the fork's server (branch `tsubaki-server`) gained a `?format=pcm` wire mode (raw PCM16 LE @ 24 kHz in the `0x01` frames, both directions), so the browser engine needs no codec at all and mirrors the fal engine almost verbatim:

- `use-moshi-session.ts` implements the shared session surface; `moshi-agent.ts` resolves per-persona `voice_prompt`/`text_prompt` into the connect URL's query params (`ws://localhost:8998/api/chat`, override via `NEXT_PUBLIC_PERSONAPLEX_WS_URL`).
- Persona conditioning (voice preset + role prompt) is shared with the fal engine via `personaplex-personas.ts` — an A/B between KYUTAI and FAL.AI varies only the serving stack.
- Full-duplex consequences as assessed: no user transcript, `interrupt()` only stops local playback, `callState` derives from output voicing (700 ms hold across pad gaps, 1.5 s quiet finalizes a transcript turn).
- The greeting mic-gate runs **server-side** (our fork, on by default); the client keeps `autoGainControl:false`. Mute streams silence — the local model's steps are input-driven, so the mic clock must never stop.
- Orchestration: `mise run personaplex-local` (kyutai RL by default; `PERSONAPLEX_HF_REPO` switches checkpoints) + `mise run dev`.

Key architectural intent:
- The UI binds to a provider-agnostic `SessionApi` (`lib/realtime/`). `provider.engine` selects the engine: absent ⇒ **mock** lifecycle; `elevenlabs` ⇒ `@elevenlabs/react` `useConversation` + `NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID`; `xai` ⇒ direct WebSocket (`use-xai-session` + `xai-audio` PCM16 + `/api/xai/token`); `openai` ⇒ **gpt-realtime-2 over WebRTC** (`use-openai-session` + `/api/openai/token`, ephemeral key → `POST /v1/realtime/calls`; WebRTC handles all audio, no PCM pipeline; input transcript via `gpt-realtime-whisper`). The two custom hooks share one interface; `use-realtime-session` picks the active one as `custom` and routes all controls through it.

OpenAI turn detection uses **`semantic_vad`** (eagerness `low` for slow personas, `medium` for snappy) after the user found energy-based `server_vad` too sensitive to room noise; the `turnDetection` type also still supports `server_vad` (threshold/silence/prefix) + `create_response`/`interrupt_response`. Verified: OpenAI accepts the semantic_vad payload (no error) and speech_started fires far less often.

content.text:
That's a precise diagnosis, and it points at a real bug in *our* client, not the server: the bundled web client plays audio through an AudioWorklet with a jitter buffer, while our `PlaybackQueue` chains `AudioBufferSourceNode`s off `onended` events. With xAI's large turn-based deltas that's inaudible — but PersonaPlex PCM mode delivers **80ms frames paced at realtime**, so every single frame boundary picks up a main-thread-latency gap (1–10ms), and any late frame underruns. That's a crackle every 80ms, greeting or not — exactly what you heard.

The fix is sample-accurate scheduling: `source.start(atExactTime)` against the context clock with a small jitter lead, instead of starting each chunk when the previous one reports ended. Let me implement it:

content.text:
The crackle was ours, not the server's — your greeting-stability fixes were applied and working all along. Fixed and objectively verified.

**Root cause:** the `PlaybackQueue` both PersonaPlex engines inherited from xAI starts each audio chunk from the previous chunk's `onended` callback — a main-thread event that fires 1–10ms late. xAI's large, turn-based deltas made that inaudible, but the local server delivers **80ms frames paced at realtime**, so every frame boundary picked up a micro-gap and any slightly-late frame underran. A click every 80ms of speech — greeting or mid-conversation, exactly as you described. (The bundled `local_web.py` client never had this problem because its AudioWorklet has a jitter buffer — which is why it sounded smoother.)

**Fix:** a new [scheduled-playback.ts](lib/realtime/scheduled-playback.ts) — every chunk is scheduled at an exact position on the `AudioContext` clock (`source.start(when)`), so consecutive chunks are sample-contiguous regardless of main-thread latency, with a 160ms jitter lead absorbing arrival jitter and a clean re-anchor on genuine underruns. Both the KYUTAI and FAL.AI engines now use it (identical stream shape); xAI keeps the old queue, where it's fine.

**Verification:** I instrumented the live page to record everything the app routes to the speakers during a real KYUTAI call — 23 seconds of voiced playback from the RL model: **zero click discontinuities** (max inter-sample step 0.123, i.e. natural speech; the click threshold is 0.15), and the single ≥30ms silence in the region is the model's own pause between its two turns, not a dropout. All gates pass, and both servers are still running.

Please give it another listen with the headset. If there's any residual roughness, the next suspect is the mic-capture side — the deprecated `ScriptProcessor` shares the audio context and can jank it when React renders block the main thread — and the fix there would be migrating capture to an `AudioWorklet`, which I'd apply to all three PCM engines at once. And note the remaining word-by-word cadence you'll still hear is the model's intrinsic delivery (the PAD-token rhythm we documented), which no client can smooth — but it should now be *clean* halting speech, not crackling.

    """Consume pending encoder/decoder results until the tokenizer goes idle.

content.text:
All three items are handled. Here's what each was:

**1. The decoder/encoder errors — fixed and committed** (`2e7c4c4` on `tsubaki-server`). rustymimi's `StreamTokenizer` runs its encoder/decoder as background Rust threads with no shutdown API; when a session ends and Python drops the tokenizer, any thread mid-send hits a closed channel and prints to stderr. Harmless, but noisy. The server now drains both result channels until the threads go idle (~100ms quiet window) before the tokenizer goes out of scope — verified with a full probe session: zero closed-channel messages, previously one at warmup plus several per session.

**2. ScriptProcessor — explained and migrated.** `ScriptProcessorNode` is the original (2011-era) Web Audio API for touching raw samples; it's been deprecated for a decade because its callback runs on the **main thread** — the same thread as React renders and GC — so any jank delays audio processing, and in bad cases glitches the whole shared `AudioContext`. Its replacement, `AudioWorklet`, runs your processing code on the dedicated realtime audio thread. All three PCM engines (KYUTAI, FAL.AI, xAI) now capture through a shared worklet: [mic-capture.js](public/worklets/mic-capture.js) accumulates the 128-sample render quanta into engine-sized chunks on the audio thread and posts them zero-copy to [mic-capture.ts](lib/realtime/mic-capture.ts), which replaced the ~50-line ScriptProcessor block in each hook. Combined with the scheduled playback from last round, there's now no audio-path code left on the main thread. All gates pass, and the live test confirms capture pumps at the exact 80ms cadence with playback still click-free.

**3. The Vesper greeting glitch — mostly the model, in two ways.** The transcript artifact (`you'` for "you're") is a known text-token display quirk we documented — the audio says the full word. "Blacklist Listening" is the more interesting one: Vesper's role prompt doesn't anchor her to a business, so the model *invents* one per session — that's PersonaPlex role-play doing what it was trained to do on an unanchored prompt. And an occasionally rough audio onset on one persona but not others is consistent with the model's stochastic opening fragments (we measured 70–360ms voiced fragments at onset in the recordings) plus the NATF0 preset's character. If Vesper's opening keeps bothering you: anchor her prompt (e.g. "You answer calls for Tsubaki…") to stop the invented names, and try a different preset (`VARF1`/`VARF3` are unexplored) in [personaplex-personas.ts](lib/realtime/personaplex-personas.ts) — both engines pick it up from the same map.

One caveat worth knowing: the worklet's chunking is now sample-exact, but if a *first* chunk of a session ever sounds clipped, the remaining suspect would be the 160ms playback lead being too tight for the greeting's first burst — bumping `leadMs` in [scheduled-playback.ts](lib/realtime/scheduled-playback.ts) to ~240 is the one-line experiment. Give it a listen when you're ready — dev server and the RL model server are both up.

content.text:
Done — all committed, and the persona mystery is solved with the fix verified live.

**How the bundled client's examples work:** nothing special — a hardcoded `{label, text}` preset array in the client JS, sent as the `text_prompt` query param on connect, exactly like our `moshi-agent.ts` does. The reliability of "Astronaut (fun)" comes from the *prompt's shape*, not the mechanism. PersonaPlex was fine-tuned on dialogues generated from two prompt template families, and it anchors hard when a prompt matches one:

- **Service:** `"You work for <X> which is a <Y> and your name is <Z>. … Information: <facts>."`
- **Discussion/role-play:** `"You enjoy having a good conversation. [Have a discussion about <topic>.] You are <role>. Your name is <Z>. <scenario>. <what to do at the open>."`

Your [astronaut-persona.txt](../personaplex-mlx/data/astronaut-persona.txt) follows the second template to the letter (opener → role → name → scenario → "you urgently ask for help") — that's why it locks in every session. Our persona prompts were style essays mentioning "Tsubaki, a realtime voice console," which pattern-matched the service family for some voices (hence support-line greetings) and left others floating (hence Vesper inventing "Blacklist Listening").

[env]
NEXT_PUBLIC_ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID = "agent_0701ksfnj6kzfg2rq4gznfpjmfx4"

# ── Tasks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Secrets (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, XAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, MISTRAL_API_KEY) live in
# fnox; `fnox exec -- …` injects them for the wrapped command (the recommended
# fnox + mise pattern). Run with `mise run dev` / `mise run stop`.
# The cascade engine's realtime STT also needs `mise run stt-proxy` (separate process).

[tasks.dev]
description = "Start the Next.js dev server (+ Mistral STT proxy) with fnox secrets loaded"
run = '''
# Start the realtime-STT proxy in the background so the cascade engine has it
# without a second terminal; tear it down when the dev server exits. Without it,
# pressing CALL on the MISTRAL provider logs a harmless but noisy
# ws://localhost:3001 ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED (STT then falls back to Web Speech).
fnox exec -- bun run scripts/mistral-stt-proxy.ts &
proxy_pid=$!
trap 'kill "$proxy_pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM
fnox exec -- bun run dev
'''

[tasks.stt-proxy]
description = "Mistral realtime-STT WebSocket proxy (adds the Bearer header the browser can't); :3001"
run = "fnox exec -- bun run scripts/mistral-stt-proxy.ts"

[tasks.stop-stt-proxy]
description = "Stop the STT proxy listening on STT_PROXY_PORT (default 3001)"
run = '''
port="${STT_PROXY_PORT:-3001}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped STT proxy on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No STT proxy running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.lm-local]
description = "Serve the local cascade LM (llama-server, gemma-4-12B QAT + MTP draft); :8001"
run = '''
# Local LM leg of the cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md). Keyless —
# config/lm-models.json's `local` backend points at this server, and --alias must
# match that entry's `model` id. MTP speculative decoding via the draft head;
# text-only (no --mmproj) and thinking off, per ~/Develop/voice-cascade/README.md.
model_dir="${LM_LOCAL_MODEL_DIR:-$HOME/Develop/voice-cascade/models/gemma-4-12B}"
llama-server \
  --model "$model_dir/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf" \
  --model-draft "$model_dir/mtp-gemma-4-12B-it.gguf" \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4 \
  -ngl 999 -fa on --jinja \
  --port "${LM_LOCAL_PORT:-8001}" \
  --alias unsloth/gemma-4-12b-it-qat-GGUF
'''

[tasks.local-stack]
description = "Serve the full local cascade stack: LM llama-server (:8001) + mlx-audio TTS/STT (:8002)"
run = '''
# One terminal for the whole on-device cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md).
# mlx-audio runs in the background, llama-server in the foreground; Ctrl-C (or
# the foreground server dying) tears both down via the trap.
mise run audio-local &
audio_pid=$!
trap 'kill "$audio_pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM
mise run lm-local
'''

[tasks.stop-local-stack]
description = "Stop both local inference servers (:8001 + :8002)"
run = '''
mise run stop-lm-local
mise run stop-audio-local
'''

[tasks.audio-local]
description = "Serve the local TTS + batch-STT legs (mlx-audio server, Voxtral); :8002"
run = '''
# Local voice legs of the cascade (docs/voxtral-local-inference.md). Keyless —
# config/voice-models.json's `local` tts/stt backends point here. Models load
# lazily on first request (TTS ~4 GB + STT ~3 GB resident thereafter).
audio_dir="${MLX_AUDIO_DIR:-$HOME/Develop/mlx-audio}"
cd "$audio_dir" && .venv/bin/python -m mlx_audio.server --port "${AUDIO_LOCAL_PORT:-8002}"
'''

[tasks.stop-audio-local]
description = "Stop the mlx-audio server listening on AUDIO_LOCAL_PORT (default 8002)"
run = '''
port="${AUDIO_LOCAL_PORT:-8002}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped mlx-audio server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No mlx-audio server running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.stop-lm-local]
description = "Stop the local LM server listening on LM_LOCAL_PORT (default 8001)"
run = '''
port="${LM_LOCAL_PORT:-8001}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped local LM server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No local LM server running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.personaplex-local]
description = "Serve local full-duplex PersonaPlex (personaplex-mlx, kyutai RL checkpoint, q8); :8998"
run = '''
# The KYUTAI provider row's engine (lib/realtime/use-moshi-session.ts) connects
# to this server at ws://localhost:8998/api/chat?format=pcm. Keyless (HF token
# from the ambient env for the gated checkpoint download, first run only).
# Switch checkpoints with PERSONAPLEX_HF_REPO=nvidia/personaplex-7b-v1.
plex_dir="${PERSONAPLEX_DIR:-$HOME/Develop/personaplex-mlx}"
cd "$plex_dir" && uv run python -u -m personaplex_mlx.local_web \
  -q 8 \
  --hf-repo "${PERSONAPLEX_HF_REPO:-kyutai/personaplex-rl-seamless}" \
  --port "${PERSONAPLEX_PORT:-8998}" \
  --no-browser
'''

[tasks.stop-personaplex-local]
description = "Stop the PersonaPlex server listening on PERSONAPLEX_PORT (default 8998)"
run = '''
port="${PERSONAPLEX_PORT:-8998}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped PersonaPlex server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No PersonaPlex server running on :$port"
fi
'''

[tasks.stop]
description = "Stop the dev server listening on PORT (default 3000)"
run = '''
port="${PORT:-3000}"
pids=$(lsof -ti tcp:"$port" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$pids" ]; then
  kill $pids && echo "Stopped dev server on :$port (PID: $pids)"
else
  echo "No dev server running on :$port"
fi
'''

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. ## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. - **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

# Browser Authentication for fal Realtime WebSocket

The documentation provides two approaches for secure browser authentication:

## Token Provider Approach (Recommended)

The exact endpoint and implementation:

**Endpoint:** `https://rest.fal.ai/tokens/realtime`

**Method:** POST

**Request body fields:**
- `allowed_apps`: Array of app paths (e.g., `["fal-ai/fast-lcm-diffusion/realtime"]`)
- `duration`: Token lifetime in seconds (e.g., 120)

**Response shape:** `{ token: string }`

**Example implementation:**

The documentation shows a Next.js route that calls this endpoint with headers including `Authorization: Key ${process.env.FAL_KEY}`. The client then uses a `tokenProvider` function that "fetches short-lived JWT tokens from your backend" to authenticate each connection.

## Proxy URL Approach

Alternatively, point your client at `proxyUrl: "/api/fal/proxy"` where a server-side proxy adds your API key before forwarding requests.

**Security note:** The documentation emphasizes you must "verify that the request comes from an authenticated user in your application" at your token endpoint to prevent unauthorized credit consumption.

— a **full-duplex** speech-to-speech model that listens while it speaks. Unlike
every other engine there is no VAD and no turn events: the model opens the call
with its own greeting, barge-in is native (just talk over it), and INTERRUPT is
effectively a no-op. There is no user-side transcript (no ASR in the path); the
agent transcript streams from the model's inner-monologue text tokens.

Transport is a direct browser→fal WebSocket
(`wss://fal.run/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime`) carrying **msgpack** binary frames
with raw PCM16 audio bytes at a fixed 24 kHz both ways (the server silently
ignores JSON text frames) — the `AudioContext` is constructed at 24 kHz so the
browser resamples at the edges. A short-lived JWT is minted server-side at
`POST /api/fal/token`; the secret `FAL_API_KEY` never reaches the client.

Keep `FAL_API_KEY` in **fnox** and run via `fnox exec -- bun run dev` /
