content.text:
Resolved. Here's the full picture:

**The codex comment was half right.** It correctly flagged that `rest.alpha.fal.ai/tokens/` is the legacy endpoint — fal's current docs use `POST https://rest.fal.ai/tokens/realtime`. But its two other claims didn't survive live testing:

- Its severity was overstated: the alpha endpoint still works (HTTP 201, and that token still authorizes the socket), so "the FAL provider cannot connect" was false.
- Its suggested request schema was wrong: the live `tokens/realtime` endpoint rejects the docs' `allowed_apps` array with HTTP 422 ("Field required: app") — it requires a **singular** owner-prefixed `app` field. I probed variants: `"fal-ai/personaplex/realtime"` and `"fal-ai/personaplex"` both mint (201); the bare alias `"personaplex"` 404s.

**The fix** ([route.ts](app/api/fal/token/route.ts), commit `72d4ff0`, pushed): migrated to `rest.fal.ai/tokens/realtime` with `{ app: "fal-ai/personaplex/realtime", duration: 300 }`, and the response normalization now accepts both the bare JSON-string JWT the endpoint actually returns and the `{ token }` shape the docs claim. A comment in the route records the docs-vs-live schema discrepancy so the next reader doesn't "fix" it back.

**Verified end-to-end:** all four gates pass (tsc, oxlint, fmt, build), and with the dev server running, `POST /api/fal/token` returned a 395-char JWT whose decoded claims are `allowed_apps: ["fal-ai/personaplex"]` — a WebSocket probe with that token connected to `wss://fal.run/fal-ai/personaplex/realtime` and stayed open (unauthorized tokens are rejected at the handshake). The review thread on [PR #11](https://github.com/jessearmand/subaki-realtime/pull/11) is marked resolved.

The dev server is still up on :3000 (via `mise run dev`, secrets loaded) if you want to place a FAL.AI call to hear it — `mise run stop` when done.

# PersonaPlex WebSocket Schema - Not Fully Documented

The documentation page provided does **not include the exact WebSocket schema** for real-time streaming. Here's what's available:

## Standard REST Input Schema (from docs):

The page specifies these fields:
- `"prompt"` (string) - "Text prompt describing the AI persona"
- `"voice"` (VoiceEnum) - defaults to `"NATF2"`
- `"voice_audio_url"` (string) - optional voice cloning
- `"audio_url"` (string) - **required**, input audio file URL
- `"temperature_audio"`, `"temperature_text"`, `"top_k_audio"`, `"top_k_text"`, `"seed"` (numeric)

## Streaming Code Example:

The documentation shows a `.stream()` method but doesn't detail WebSocket field naming:

```javascript
const stream = await fal.stream("fal-ai/personaplex", {
  input: { audio_url: "https://..." }
});
```

## Gap in Documentation:

The page lacks specifics on:
- Exact WebSocket field names (whether `prompt` vs `text_prompt`)
- Real-time audio chunk format/encoding
- Configuration message structure for streaming connections

**Recommendation:** Check the [Schema reference](/api/openapi/queue/openapi.json?endpoint_id=fal-ai/personaplex) or contact fal.ai support for complete WebSocket protocol details.

content.text:
The gates all pass. The cold-start probe is still idling (it waits 10 minutes so fal's container actually goes cold, then listens for 90 seconds) — I'll report its result and commit when it fires. Here's where the diagnosis stands:

**Your two observations have one root cause each, and neither is a missing prompt:**

1. **"Zero prompts" in the request history is a logging artifact.** For realtime sessions, fal logs the *connection* as the request — the prompt/voice/sampling config rides inside every msgpack binary frame, which the dashboard doesn't decode or display. The prompt is definitely reaching the model: every probe greeting referenced the persona ("Hello, welcome to Tsubaki. How can I help you today?" — that text exists nowhere but our config).

2. **The missing greetings are cold starts.** Probing the live socket with client-identical traffic: a cold container returned *nothing* in 20 seconds; the next connection took 11.2s to first audio; warm connections take ~5s. A cold fal worker has to load the 7B model before it can speak — likely 30–60s+ — and a session you give up on shows up in history as one of those empty requests. The local MLX server never has this problem because the model stays resident, which is consistent with your earlier "fal greeting often not played, local much more responsive" comparison.

**Client fixes made in [use-fal-session.ts](lib/realtime/use-fal-session.ts)** (gates pass, not yet committed):
- Removed the zero-length "kick" frame sent on socket open — `audio` is a required non-empty binary in fal's realtime schema, so it was invalid, and it did nothing useful since the mic worklet's silence chunks already drive the session.
- On connect, the caption now says "connected — model warming up (a cold start can take a minute)…" instead of a dead-sounding "listening…", so a cold start reads as warming up rather than a broken call.

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
Serverless GPU inference has a warm-pool economics problem that full-duplex voice makes brutal: a text API can hide a 30s cold start behind a spinner, but a voice call that opens with 30s of silence reads as *broken*. Providers usually solve it with pinned/reserved capacity (fal calls this "machines kept warm"), which trades idle cost for latency — exactly the trade your local MLX server makes by keeping the model resident in memory all day.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

One decision worth yours: if cold starts confirm at 30s+, do you want a **pre-warm ping** — briefly opening (or queue-pinging) the fal app when the FAL.AI provider row is *selected*, so the container is warm by the time you press CALL? It costs a few compute-seconds per warm-up and would make the first call feel like the local server. I'll hold off unless you want it.

content.text:
It's not a bug in our hooks — it's architectural to PersonaPlex, on both engines. There is no ASR anywhere in the path, so the user's speech never becomes text at any point.

**What the text stream actually is.** PersonaPlex is a Moshi-architecture model: every 80ms frame it jointly samples audio tokens *and one text token* — the "inner monologue" ([docs](docs/personaplex-local-inference.md:62)). That text stream is aligned exclusively with **the model's own speech** — it's what the model is about to say, emitted just ahead of its audio. Your mic audio enters the model as raw Mimi audio tokens on the *input* stream and is consumed directly for understanding; the model never produces a textual rendering of it. So the server (fal or local, same model) sends exactly one kind of text: agent text. That's why both hooks only ever create `who: "agent"` turns — [use-fal-session.ts:289](lib/realtime/use-fal-session.ts:289) pushes every `msg.text` as an agent delta, and [use-moshi-session.ts:218](lib/realtime/use-moshi-session.ts:218) does the same for `0x02` text frames. There's no user-turn code path because the protocol has nothing to feed it. NVIDIA's own bundled web client behaves identically: it shows only the model's monologue.

**Why the other providers do show your words:** ElevenLabs, xAI, and OpenAI realtime are (or embed) cascaded systems — their servers run ASR on your audio as part of the pipeline and emit explicit user-transcription events over the protocol. PersonaPlex skips ASR entirely; that's precisely where its low latency and native barge-in come from.

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
The inner monologue isn't a transcript feature — it's a *quality* mechanism. Forcing the model to commit to a text token before the matching audio tokens anchors its speech in language-model reasoning (Moshi's ablations show factuality and coherence drop without it). The user-side text you see from other providers is a separate ASR product; in a true speech-to-speech model, "understanding you" happens in audio-token space and leaves no textual trace to display.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

If you want user turns in the transcript for these two providers, it has to be a **client-side ASR sidecar** feeding off the mic chunks we already capture in the AudioWorklet. The repo already owns two candidates from the cascade engine: the Mistral realtime STT proxy (`scripts/mistral-stt-proxy.ts`, :3001) and the local mlx-audio batch STT (:8002), plus Silero VAD for utterance segmentation. Tapping the existing capture callback means zero extra mic plumbing — the chunks would just be teed to STT and pushed as `who: "user"` turns. Happy to wire that if you want it; for a pure A/B of the two PersonaPlex stacks, the transcript asymmetry with other providers may even be worth keeping visible.

Meanwhile the cold-start probe fired and confirmed the theory hard: after 10 minutes idle, a connection got **zero response in 90 seconds** — the container didn't even finish warming in that window. So a first call after idle genuinely has no greeting for 1.5+ minutes, which is exactly your "empty request" rows. The client fix (no invalid kick frame + honest "warming up" caption) is staged; I'll hold the commit in case you want the STT sidecar bundled in.

fal.ai PersonaPlex realtime facts (probe-verified 2026-07-20, may drift):

- **Token mint**: `POST https://rest.fal.ai/tokens/realtime` requires a SINGULAR
  owner-prefixed `app` field + `duration` — the docs' `allowed_apps` array 422s
  ("Field required: app"). Returns a bare JSON-string JWT despite docs showing
  `{token}`. Legacy `rest.alpha.fal.ai/tokens/` still works but is deprecated.
- **Request history logs empty inputs for realtime sessions** — the persona
  config rides inside every msgpack frame and is never shown in the dashboard.
  "Zero prompts" there is a logging artifact, not a missing-prompt bug.
- **Cold starts**: first connection after a long idle can return nothing for
  20s+; warm connections greet in ~5s. Keep-warm window exceeds 10 min idle.
- **`audio` is a required non-empty binary** in the realtime input schema —
  never send a zero-length bootstrap frame; continuous mic (silence) chunks
  drive the session.
- PersonaPlex has **no user-side ASR**: the text stream is the model's inner
  monologue for its OWN speech only, so a user transcript requires a
  client-side STT sidecar (deferred; candidates: [[realtime-persona-overview]]
  cascade's Mistral STT proxy or local mlx-audio STT).
